idiom_name: class DirView(raw: Dir) : Dir by raw, with mediated members overridden
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes the forwarding half declarative: in `class DirView(private val raw: Dir) : Dir by raw` the compiler generates every member of Dir that forwards to raw, and any member you override replaces the generated forwarding, which is where the membrane wraps arguments, checks revocation and wraps results (kotlinlang.org). That means the mediated surface is exactly the set of overridden members: delegation replaces the classic per-member forwarding code, but it does not intercept anything itself, so a member left un-overridden is a raw route through the membrane. This variant is right for a small, explicit mediated surface where static type checking of the wrapper matters; use the JVM dynamic proxy variant when the surface is large or evolving and every call must pass through one handler.
pitfalls: `by raw` forwards every member the class does not override, so mediating a subset leaves the rest of the interface as a raw route - the delegation syntax makes the omission invisible in review.
The delegate is stored in a synthesized field reachable through reflection/Kotlin reflection, so an in-process guest with reflective access can read the raw reference and reach around the membrane.

`by` captures the delegate at construction: revocation must be a flag the overridden members check, not a re-pointed delegate, since swapping it would require the delegate to be a var surface the compiler does not generate.

variants.name: JVM dynamic proxy via java.lang.reflect.Proxy (total mediation)
variants.idiom_name: Proxy.newProxyInstance with an InvocationHandler performing the wrapping
variants.implementation_notes: On the JVM, Kotlin can borrow Java's dynamic proxy: Proxy.newProxyInstance(...) returns an object implementing the requested interfaces whose every call lands in one InvocationHandler, so the membrane has a single place to check revocation, wrap arguments and wrap the result regardless of how large the interface is (docs.oracle.com). This is the total-mediation counterpart to the `by` variant: nothing can be forwarded unmediated because the handler sees all calls, including equals/hashCode/toString - which the handler must delegate to the target itself. The price is reflection dispatch per call, interfaces only, and a proxy whose static type is the interface while its runtime identity is a generated class.
pitfalls: The handler receives equals, hashCode and toString too; delegating them to the target is required or proxies break as map keys and in comparisons, and forgetting it makes the membrane change collection behaviour.

Dynamic proxies need interfaces: a final class target cannot be proxied this way, and method handles obtained from the proxy capture the handler, so identity maps and memos must be keyed on the target, not the proxy.
Exceptions arrive wrapped in InvocationTargetException, and every call pays a reflective dispatch - the cost of total mediation where no hook otherwise exists.
